judges.description: LLM-as-judge graders for datasets whose answer is free text, where no deterministic matcher can grade a cell. Each value names a registered judge (`promptpotter.judges`) and the models to run it on; its verdict is banked as a per-sample observation the `scoring` formula reads. **The KEY is the term that formula reads, not the judge's name** — so one cell can carry several graded terms, which is what a multi-step schema (retrieve -> ground -> answer) is, and two terms may run the same rubric on different models without one verdict landing on top of the other. Declaration order is the step order. Swapping a judge invalidates every verdict taken under the old one, so a resume must run divergence detection rather than carry them forward. **Their models are declared here and inherited from nowhere** — not from the permitted model set, not from the pipeline's node config, not from the optimizer's own LLMs. A judge is a ruler, and a ruler that moved with whatever the search was last steered to would not be one.

A steer outside it is a `campaign.babysit` act — warned + graded C (`steer_verdict`, asked when a fork's seed is parsed). Nothing declared for a node = nothing sanctioned there, the restrictive default.

Candidate breadth is paid per candidate, per round. Every comparison downstream is matched by sample key or θ-space, so an origin scored on a superset stays like-for-like. A bank smaller than this scores on the whole bank (`sample_dataset` is a prefix slice) — not an error.

ConfigEdit.description:
A check-in edit's ``config``, by `CampaignConfig`'s own paths. Only the fields sent move
anything: its ``exclude_unset`` dump is the layer `campaign_config.py::merge_config_layers`

accuracy_ceiling.description: The accuracy a best-reachable prompt would score on this dataset at this campaign's model. `index.json::final.rounds_to_ceiling` counts rounds against `CEILING_FRACTION` of it, and the value is banked beside that count so a reader never has to guess the denominator. `None` (default) → the clock reports nothing, which is the honest reading: a ceiling is a joint claim about the dataset AND the model, so only the dataset owner can declare one (`dataset.yaml::campaign`) and a guessed value makes every campaign on it publish a round count nobody can defend. DISPLAY config — it moves no gate, no selection and no stop.
accuracy_ceiling.title: Accuracy Ceiling

bench_trigger.description: When the line's bench passes are sent — each a cell per bench row, the ranked `dataset_split.bench` and every bench-only row the bank declares. `manual` (default): a launch sends none and sets nothing aside for one; the operator asks for the headline (CLI `bench`, command `grade-bench`), which grades the origin and the selection as they then stand. `at_end`: the origin's pass at launch, its price set aside under the ceiling, and the selection's once the run ends. `each_round`: that, and every round that selects a new individual is graded too. An arm of a head-to-head is minted `at_end` where this says `manual`: its comparison is the bench score.
bench_trigger.title: Bench Trigger

dataset_split.description: How run init partitions the bank into the search split every optimizer draw reads, the held-out bench set the headline is scored on, and a demo pool. `None` holds nothing out: the whole bank is the search split and there is no bench score.

display_metric.description: Which fitness number the operator's round and candidate views display first (lineage node value, Best tile, sidebar). DISPLAY config, not search state — the optimizer's selector decides on its own objective, and the campaign's headline is the bench score; this only picks the number the human READS, client-overridable per session. `ability` shows θ (a logit, jargon) where the selector stamps one — defaults to `accuracy` so θ is never forced on an operator who didn't ask for it. Rides the `composite_fitness_formula` serve path to `dashboard.json::display_metric`; never on `OptSearchPoint`.

hard_sample_order.description: Which key ranks the hard-sample leaderboard — the heatmap, the table and the `log.md` heatmap, which all read ONE served rank. `info_gain` sorts by the queue mechanism's acquisition score (`pick_value`: decision-information gain + δ learning gain) read on the cycle's ruler at the frontier's stamped ability, contested-at-the-frontier samples first; `difficulty` sorts by the ruler's δ_s alone, hardest first, and is what a scope with no stamped ability (dataset scope) is served whatever this says. DISPLAY config: it picks the order the human READS and never what the engine scores, which is `build_round_order` and reaches no knob. Client-overridable per session, like `display_metric`.
hard_sample_order.title: Hard Sample Order

judges.description: LLM-as-judge graders for datasets whose answer is free text, where no deterministic matcher can grade a cell. Each value names a registered judge (`promptpotter.judges`) and the models to run it on; its verdict is banked as a per-sample observation the `scoring` formula reads. **The KEY is the term that formula reads, not the judge's name** — so one cell can carry several graded terms, which is what a multi-step schema (retrieve -> ground -> answer) is, and two terms may run the same rubric on different models without one verdict landing on top of the other. Declaration order is the step order. Swapping a judge invalidates every verdict taken under the old one, so a resume must run divergence detection rather than carry them forward. **Their models are declared here and inherited from nowhere** — not from the permitted model set, not from the pipeline's node config, not from the optimizer's own LLMs. A judge is a ruler, and a ruler that moved with whatever the search was last steered to would not be one.
judges.title: Judges

optimizer_narrowing.description: Per-node declaration over the dataset's optimizer search space — the per-campaign param-lock + value-space lever beside `exclude_nodes` (whole node). `provider`/`route_order` are always locked. **`param_keys` SUBSETS the config axes, `prompt_fields_held` holds the prompt fields it names, and `param_allowed_values` REPLACES** (`PipelineSchema.narrow`, applied at pipeline setup): a campaign may only close axes the dataset opened, but the value space is its own statement — which is what lets an operator ADD a model or a reasoning rung no `dataset.yaml::pipeline` on disk carries. `param_allowed_values['model']` is also the ONE permitted model set: what the optimizer may pick, and what a human fork may steer to without tainting the branch. A steer outside it is a `campaign.babysit` act — warned + graded C (`steer_verdict`, asked when a fork's seed is parsed). Nothing declared for a node = nothing sanctioned there, the restrictive default.
optimizer_narrowing.title: Optimizer Narrowing

run_seed.description: The run's one seed. It seeds which rows fall where and the order the search pool reads in: each row ranks by this and its content (`Sample.key`), never its slot, so a reordered bank holds out the same rows and reads them in the same order. An L4 seat seeds its determinism clamp and its solver node from it too.
run_seed.title: Run Seed

sp_budget_origin.description: Origin eval budget — how many bank samples the origin (C0) is scored on at check-in. The bench's, whatever the optimizer: a round's own panel is its sampler's knob. Wide because origin breadth is the one breadth that is nearly free: θ_origin is the term EVERY delta subtracts, and its rows are content-addressed cache replayed into every candidate arm, fork and resume — paid once per config. Candidate breadth is paid per candidate, per round. Every comparison downstream is matched by sample key or θ-space, so an origin scored on a superset stays like-for-like. A bank smaller than this scores on the whole bank (`sample_dataset` is a prefix slice) — not an error.
sp_budget_origin.title: Sp Budget Origin

One cell of a 2-D projection — every subject sharing a (row, column) coordinate, pooled.

Served rather than left to the browser for the reason every other number here is: a cell
holding three subjects IS an aggregate, and a surface that averaged them would re-answer under
its own guess at the weighting (``webapp/CLAUDE.md`` § Scoring authority).

FactorGridReading.description:
The 2-D face of the factor cube that the reader asked for.

A face rather than the cube, permanently. A third factor does not need a third visual
dimension; it needs a decision about what happens to it, and there are exactly two — it is
MARGINALISED (pooled into the values here) or it is FIXED (dropped from the selection). Both
leave a flat grid, so five factors cost the same surface as two and no display dimension is
ever added — which is also why a fourth factor raises no new question. ``marginalised`` names
what was collapsed, because a cell silently pooling over an axis the reader forgot about is the
one way this panel could mislead.

A projection is REQUESTED rather than served for every pair: a roster varying on fifteen keys
holds 105 of them, and the reader is looking at one.

FactorLevel.description:

mean of their means, so a subject that measured twice as many cells carries twice the weight it
earned. ``None`` where the factor is not poolable, or where a level holds no scored cell; a
surface renders that as absent rather than as zero.
FactorLevel.title: FactorLevel

FactorReading.description:
One factor the selection varies on, with its levels — the axis half of a factorial read.

Factors are DISCOVERED, never declared: a key that every subject answers identically is not a
factor, it is a constant, and the operator should not have to name what the roster already
shows. Discovery spans the dataset each subject ran on and the resolved config it ran under,
which are two keyspaces and one question.

Whether the ``value`` column may be pooled is a property of the METRIC against the roster
rather than of this factor: see :data:`_POOLABLE_UNITS`. Where it may not, the levels and their
membership stay intact — grouping is always honest, only the aggregate is not — every
``value`` is null and ``note`` says why, so a surface can still lay the grid out.

``confounded_with`` is the one that decides whether a marginal may be BELIEVED, and it is why
this is a reading rather than a group-by. A roster assembled from campaigns that already ran is
observational, not a designed grid: nothing balanced it, so two factors can cut the subjects
into the identical partition and their marginals are then the same number wearing two names.
Measured, on five banked campaigns: ``agent.model`` split 292.2s against 58.5s and was aliased
exactly by ``dataset``, so the "slower model" was the harbor bank. Naming the alias is the
whole defence — a surface can gray the column, and a reader who fixes one of the pair gets an
honest contrast on the other.

arm_gate.description: Hold every round, before any arm is measured, until the operator answers with the arms it measures (`submit-arms`). ``off`` (default) never holds. ``review``: the proposers run, their proposals are drafts, and the operator keeps any of them by index, adds arms of their own, or both. ``author``: no proposer runs and every arm is the operator's. An arm of theirs is an edit of the round's parent — prompt fields, a pipeline overlay — and is measured and elected like any other. The hold has no deadline; a pause ends it resumably, and a resume holds again unless an answer was already banked.

budget.description: The campaign's own layer of the run's budget. ``usd`` / ``tokens`` bound the CAMPAIGN's cumulative spend (optimizer + backend), shared by its live cycles and checked at the next boundary; ``rounds`` caps one cycle's closed rounds after the origin (0 measures the origin and stops; null leaves only ``HARD_CAP_ARMS``); ``wall_clock_s`` bounds one launch, cutting a remote cell still open at its edge. A fork seed, a standing ``set-limits`` and a launch flag each lay over it axis by axis, and the account admits the result whole or refuses the launch. A null axis is unbounded. ``tokens`` is unset by default: a token is worth a different amount on every route, so set it only where a backend bills but reports no cost (``unpriced_tokens`` on the dashboard is the tell).

convergence_patience.description: Consecutive closed rounds without an advance of the best-so-far line on the origin panel (``RunStanding.rounds_without_advance``) after which the run stops ``converged``, under any optimizer. A promotion resets it, separated from the origin or not; a round whose origin-panel reading was not taken counts neither way. ``None`` → no such stop.

degradation_fatal_fastpath.description: End a candidate at the first FATAL sample (empty response, content-filtered, structurally broken) without spending the rest of its budget. Active while the degradation check runs (`degradation_threshold` > 0); the rate-based check stays governed by that threshold. The bench's, run on every optimizer's arms.

determinism.description: Pin the optimizer's decoding and its route so a re-run reproduces this campaign's trajectory and can name the host that produced each number. `None` (default) → every node runs at its own file settings and the gateway routes per call. judges.description: LLM-as-judge graders for datasets whose answer is free text, where no deterministic matcher can grade a cell. Declaration order is the step order. A steer outside it is a `campaign.babysit` act — warned + graded C (`steer_verdict`, asked when a fork's seed is parsed). Nothing declared for a node = nothing sanctioned there, the restrictive default.

RankedEdit.description:
One SEARCHPOINT measured against its own campaign's origin — a prompt edit, a node-config
edit, an optimizer-prompt edit on the recursion; the arithmetic does not care which.

**The identity is ``sp_hash``**, the archive join already stamped on every candidate row, so a
prose-only edit ranks like any other. Keying the sparse ``pipeline_overlay`` instead cannot see
one at all: that overlay is empty for a prompt-only candidate, which is the whole of what L1
proposes on a campaign optimizing prompts.

**Rows POOL WITHIN ONE CAMPAIGN and never across two.** A
searchpoint is read through a delta against its parent, and two campaigns share no parent to
take one against — so a cross-campaign pool is a number lined up on nothing, and that is a
claim withdrawn rather than a capability lost. Do not re-add it as an improvement. Within one
campaign the pool is real: individuals sharing a searchpoint share its cells, which are filed
by content, so they are one member of the pair.

reading.description: The searchpoint over its campaign's origin under the selected metric, on the cells both scored. Its headline's `family` is Holm across the edits ranked here. An edit whose reading is not `read` is listed after them, unranked.

RunPhase.description:

- ``queued``: a launch claimed the cycle and waits for a machine slot.
- ``starting``: a claimed launch past the queue, its process coming up.
- ``running``: a process is attached and driving the cycle.
- ``scoring``: a paid pass (bench, verify, noise floor) holds the cycle outside its loop.

parameters.description:
Subjects to pool, one per repetition of the parameter: `campaign:<campaign_id>` (its root origin), `course:<campaign_id>/<cycle_id>` (one branch, read at its last elected winner) or `candidate:<campaign_id>/<cycle_id>/<candidate_id>` (one searchpoint). May span campaigns and datasets, which the comparability verdict then reports on.

An L4 inner run is addressed like any other, plus the sandbox chain it lives in: `;in=<campaign>::<cycle>`, root-first and `~`-joined, the same codec as `?descend=` because it is the same question. A sandbox is structurally an ordinary projects tree, so every kind above resolves inside one unchanged.

A MASK rides the address, `;`-separated, so the record and the counterfactual can be two channels of one read: `;samples=3,7,11` restricts every value to those samples, and `;lens=score:<formula>` (courses only) re-decides the branch's elections under another criterion and reads it at the winner that would have stood. The response carries what that changed in `subjects[].scenario`, worded once as `scenario.said`, its caveat the said's detail.
